nodes.name: threat-intel-daily.js
nodes.description: Daily threat intelligence scanner that collects all workspace packages, queries threat feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA), cross-references findings, and sends Telegram alerts for critical/high issues.
responsibilities: Recursively discover all package.json files in workspace
Collect installed package names and versions
Fetch threat intelligence from multiple feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA, GitHub Advisories)
Query OSV API for version-specific vulnerability lookups
Enrich findings with full summaries from OSV API
Cross-reference threats against installed packages
Separate infrastructure threats (CISA KEV/OS CVEs) from npm/pypi vulnerabilities
Track new findings vs. previous scans to avoid alert fatigue
Send Telegram alerts for critical/high severity findings
Save comprehensive JSON report to data/threat-intel-report.json
inputs: config/config.json for API keys and settings
.env file for Telegram bot token and chat ID
outputs: JSON report at data/threat-intel-report.json with: timestamp, packages scanned, severity breakdown, matches with details, infrastructure threats
Telegram message to configured chat (if configured and findings exist)
Console output with 5-step scan progress and summary
algorithm_steps: 1. Find all package.json files (max depth 5, skip node_modules/.git/dist/build/.next/__pycache__)
2. Collect installed packages with versions from dependencies and devDependencies
3. Fetch threat feeds (OSV, NVD, CISA, GitHub Advisories) for last 7 days
4. Query OSV API for version-specific vulnerabilities in installed packages
5. Enrich findings with full summaries (parallel fetch, concurrency 10)
6. Cross-reference feed findings against installed packages
7. Deduplicate findings and separate npm/pypi from OS/infrastructure CVEs
8. Load previous report to detect new findings and avoid repeat alerts
9. Send Telegram alert if critical/high severity or new findings detected
nodes.threat_separation: npm/pypi vulnerabilities stored in 'matches' array; OS CVEs/CISA KEV threats stored in 'infrastructureThreats' array to prevent confusion with package vulnerabilities
nodes.alert_logic: Sends alert if: critical severity exists, high severity exists, new critical/high finding detected since last scan, or new CISA KEV threat detected

layers.name: Entry Points & CLI
layers.description: Command-line interfaces and automation scripts that trigger scans and coordinate the scanning workflow. Primary entry point through src/index.js, plus specialized CLI utilities for batch scanning, dependency analysis, and integration with deployment systems.

layers.name: Orchestration & Decision Engine
layers.description: Core logic that coordinates security scanners and produces threat verdicts. The GuardDog class orchestrates all scanner modules in sequence, while the DecisionTree synthesizes all threat signals (VirusTotal votes, reputation scores, CVE findings, pattern matches, threat intelligence) into risk classifications: BARK (danger, >=100), WHINE (suspicious, 50-99), or SILENT (safe, <50). Provides both src/core/ structured versions and flat src/ module copies for compatibility.

layers.name: Security Scanners
layers.description: Threat detection modules that analyze packages for security vulnerabilities and suspicious behavior. Includes VirusTotal antivirus API integration, CVE/OSV vulnerability database queries, package reputation aggregation across npm/PyPI/GitHub/RubyGems, static code pattern analysis for malware detection, and multi-source threat intelligence collection. Contains both src/scanners/ structured versions and src/ flat module copies.

layers.name: Alerts & Notification System
layers.description: Notification delivery and external system integration. Sends Telegram bot alerts for dangerous packages (BARK verdicts), formats rich alert messages with threat details, and manages bot API communication. Includes both src/alerts/ structured version and src/ flat module copy.

layers.name: Infrastructure & Operations
layers.description: System-level operations, health monitoring, setup automation, and background task management. Includes SSH tunnel health checks with recovery (dittofeed, job-queue, postiz tunnels), threat intelligence daily refresh from public feeds, vulnerability database sync, git hook installation/removal, npm postinstall triggers, log consolidation, and interactive setup wizards. Low-level support for data directories, path resolution, and ESM module loading.

layers.name: Configuration & Policy
layers.description: Configuration files and policy definitions. Includes API endpoint URLs and timeouts (VirusTotal, npm, PyPI, GitHub, RubyGems), decision thresholds for verdict classification, trusted provider allowlist for fast-pass scanning, npm package manifest with CLI binaries and scripts, environment secrets template, and batch scan example payloads.

layers.name: Documentation & Reference
layers.description: User guides, operations manuals, and project documentation. Includes public README with installation and usage, project context and tech stack, operations manual with logging and retention policies, security disclosure policy, Claude Code agent configuration with verdict levels, skill command definition, and index for navigation.

layers.name: Tests & Quality Assurance
layers.description: Unit and integration test suite covering all major scanner modules, decision logic, alert formatting, scan history persistence, and batch analysis workflows.

tour.languageLesson: Configuration is externalized in JSON files, making thresholds tunable without code changes. This is a common DevOps pattern.

tour.title: Main CLI Entry Point
tour.description: Explore src/index.js, the main CLI orchestrator. This is where command parsing, subcommand routing, and overall flow control happen.
tour.languageLesson: The CLI uses process.argv parsing and subcommands (analyze, batch, doctor, etc.). It coordinates multiple scanner modules into a pipeline.

tour.title: Guard-Dog Core Orchestrator
tour.description: Review src/core/guard-dog.js (or src/core/guard-dog.js for the newer modular version). This class initializes all scanners and coordinates the scanning flow.
tour.languageLesson: GuardDog uses constructor dependency injection, initializing VirusTotal, Reputation, CVE, and Pattern modules. Error handling gracefully degrades if a module fails.

tour.title: Scanner 1: CVE Checking
tour.description: Learn how Guard-Dog checks for known vulnerabilities using the OSV (Open Source Vulnerabilities) API. CVE detection is fundamental to the threat model.
tour.languageLesson: CVE checking queries external APIs (OSV, GitHub, NVD). It demonstrates HTTP client patterns and rate-limit handling in JavaScript.

tour.title: Scanner 2: Reputation Analysis
tour.description: Explore src/reputation-checker.js, which analyzes package metadata from npm, PyPI, GitHub, and RubyGems. Reputation is a key threat signal.
tour.languageLesson: Reputation checking aggregates data from multiple registries. It uses heuristics like download count, star count, and maintainer activity to score trustworthiness.

tour.title: Scanner 3: Pattern Analysis
tour.description: Review src/pattern-analyzer.js, which detects malicious code patterns in package metadata and code snippets. Covers 30+ suspicious patterns.
tour.languageLesson: Pattern detection uses regex matching and string analysis. It's fast (no external calls) and catches obvious typosquatting, obfuscation, and known malware signatures.

tour.title: Scanner 4: VirusTotal Integration
tour.description: Study src/scanners/virustotal-scanner.js. This optional but powerful module scans package payloads against 70+ antivirus engines.
tour.languageLesson: VirusTotal integration uses the v3 API, handles rate limits, and gracefully degrades when the API key is missing. Shows proper error recovery patterns.

tour.title: Scanner 5: Threat Intelligence
tour.description: Review src/scanners/threat-intel.js, which aggregates threat feeds and caches known malicious packages. An optional but valuable enhancement.
tour.languageLesson: Threat Intel demonstrates caching patterns and feed aggregation. It trades network calls for disk I/O, improving performance for repeated scans.

tour.title: Decision Tree & Verdict Logic
tour.description: Examine src/core/decision-tree.js. This module combines all scanner results into a single threat score and produces BARK/WHINE/SILENT verdicts.
tour.languageLesson: Decision logic uses weighted scoring: threat scores from each scanner are aggregated, thresholds applied, and confidence calculated. This is a classic ML-style pipeline in pure JavaScript.

tour.title: Alerts & Notifications
tour.description: Review src/alerts/telegram-alert.js to understand how Guard-Dog sends alerts. When a package gets BARK, a Telegram notification fires automatically.
tour.languageLesson: Telegram alerts use async/await patterns and HTTP requests. They demonstrate safe error handling when the bot token is missing or the API is unavailable.

tour.title: Dependency Scanning
tour.description: Explore bin/scan-deps.js, which scans all dependencies in a package.json file. Used by npm hooks and git pre-commit hooks.
tour.languageLesson: scan-deps.js shows how to parse package.json, extract dependencies, and batch-scan them. It also supports --changed-only for incremental scanning.

tour.title: Nightly Automated Scanning
tour.description: Study bin/nightly-scan.js, which recursively finds all package.json files in a workspace and scans them nightly. Demonstrates recursive file discovery and task orchestration.
tour.languageLesson: Nightly scanning is recursive directory traversal with depth limits, respecting a skip list (node_modules, .git, etc.). It uses spawnSync to run child processes and collect exit codes.

tour.title: Architecture & Data Flow
tour.description: Synthesize what you've learned: trace a scan request from CLI entry point through all scanners to decision tree to verdict output. Review CONTEXT.md for a high-level architecture summary.
tour.languageLesson: The scanner pipeline is: CLI parse -> load config -> initialize modules -> scan package -> aggregate scores -> decide verdict -> alert. Each stage is independent and can fail gracefully.

tour.title: Customization & Extension
tour.description: Learn how to customize Guard-Dog: modify decision thresholds in config.json, whitelist packages in trusted-providers.json, or add new scanners to the orchestrator.
tour.languageLesson: Guard-Dog is designed for extension: new scanners can be added to GuardDog.constructor(), and new decision rules can be added to DecisionTree.evaluate().

tour.title: Testing & Validation
tour.description: Review the test suite (npm test) and understand how Guard-Dog validates its scanners. Testing is crucial for a security tool.
tour.languageLesson: Tests should cover: scanner correctness, decision tree logic, API fallbacks (when services are down), and edge cases (malformed JSON, rate limits, etc.).

tour.title: Operations & Deployment
tour.description: Review OPERATIONS.md and MANIFEST.md for how Guard-Dog is deployed and operated at scale. Covers cron jobs, logging, and production readiness.
tour.languageLesson: Production operations cover: log rotation, state directory management, error recovery, and metrics collection. Guard-Dog uses a user-writable ~/.guardog directory so global installs work safely.

tour.title: Security Considerations
tour.description: Study SECURITY.md to understand how Guard-Dog itself is built securely. This includes API key management, privilege boundaries, and audit logging.
tour.languageLesson: Security for a security tool matters: never log API keys, validate all external input, use HTTPS for API calls, and document assumptions about trust.

tour.title: Full Codebase Tour Complete
tour.description: Congratulations! You've reviewed the Guard-Dog architecture end-to-end. Now pick a feature to implement (new scanner, new alert channel, new decision rule) and dive deeper.
tour.languageLesson: To extend Guard-Dog: 1) write your feature in a new module, 2) integrate it into GuardDog.constructor(), 3) add tests, 4) update config.json if it needs new settings, 5) run the full test suite before committing.
